answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, like a sparrow that must gather shale before it can nest. The stake is slashed when peers prove an identity is fake, so an attacker pays real capital for every fake identity while honest agents get theirs back. A public lantern of signed reputation from past counterparties makes fresh cheap identities worthless, because trust must be earned over time, not minted.
